# aot-warning-baseline — the committed trim/AOT diagnostic inventory for
# `apps/Harbor.App.Cli` published with `-p:HarborWithAot=true` on linux-x64.
#
# OWNER: issue #413. Read by tools/aot-publish-gate.py; every row is a
# permission, and every row is re-probed against a real publish on every PR, so
# a row for a diagnostic nothing emits fails (delete it in the same diff).
#
# FORMAT (one row, 5 '|'-separated fields):
#
#   ID | count | verdict | first-party files | reason
#
#   ID              an IL2xxx (trim) or IL3xxx (AOT) diagnostic id. IL0xxx
#                   compiler diagnostics are out of scope: they are errors
#                   already, via TreatWarningsAsErrors in Directory.Build.props,
#                   and a publish that emitted one never reached the gate.
#   count           exact number of occurrences in the publish log. A change in
#                   either direction fails. This is NOT a threshold.
#   verdict         ACCEPTED = tolerated, with the reason in the last field.
#                   REJECTED = a bug to fix, not a concession to carry; a
#                   REJECTED row that is still emitted FAILS the gate, because
#                   it means the fix has not landed.
#   files           '-' when every site is third-party; otherwise the
#                   comma-separated first-party files (src/…, apps/…) that
#                   warn. A new first-party file fails even at an unchanged
#                   count. Line numbers are deliberately absent: a baseline
#                   keyed on lines churns on every unrelated edit and would be
#                   deleted. The log artifact carries the exact sites.
#   reason          >= 40 characters, not a bare URL. The floor and the URL
#                   rule are the same ones tests/Harbor.Architecture.Tests/
#                   ExemptionReason.cs applies to every other table in this
#                   repo, so there is one definition of "states a reason".
#
# STATE ON dev: EMPTY. #413 lands this file with no rows and the first CI run
# is expected to be RED with a NEW-row report per diagnostic id; the rows are
# then transcribed from that log, with a real count and a real reason each.
# An empty inventory is a claim that the publish emits nothing in scope, and
# the gate is what decides whether that claim survives. Do not pre-fill this
# file with guessed counts.
#
# A note on what the four IDs in apps/Harbor.App.Cli's AOT block mean here:
# that block DEMOTES them (WarningsNotAsErrors), so they do not fail the
# publish — but they are still printed, and this inventory is the record of
# them. The block's AotBlockDemotionRules table in tests/Harbor.Architecture.
# Tests/ is what keeps the csproj and this file describing the same set.
